messages:
maya-k: Quick update — ran longtail recall sweep on helix-embed-xt (int8/per-channel) against baseline helix-embed-fp16. Summary: recall@1 -0.6%, recall@10 -2.8%, recall@100 -1.2%. Cluster purity (k=50) ~ unchanged. attaching charts in a sec :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya-k: test set = 50k queries sampled from prod logs (90-day window), stratified by query freq deciles (heavy->longtail). left seed=42. used exact-sim baseline (cosine) + knn=10.

samir: curious — what's the longtail slice definition? bottom 3 deciles?

maya-k: yes, deciles 8-10 treated as longtail. actual distribution: top decile ~45% of traffic, bottom 3 deciles ~6%.

li-li: can we see the stratified SQL? might be biasing toward sessions with embeddings present.

maya-k: paste:
```
SELECT q.id, q.text
FROM queries q
JOIN (SELECT decile, count(*) FROM queries GROUP BY decile) d USING (decile)
WHERE decile >= 8
ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 50000
```

eva: hmm sampling looks fine. Did you gate on query length? longtail often = short queries which kill recall.

maya-k: yes — we kept length distribution identical to prod by sampling within (len_buckets). short queries (<=4 tokens) are 32% of longtail slice.

samir: what about centroid shift? any mean vector drift after quant?

maya-k: measured cosine centroid shift per-cluster — mean shift = 0.0023, stdev=0.0011. Not large. but a few clusters (n=7) showed >0.01 shift; investigating.

li-li: share top offending cluster ids and sample queries? I can eyeball.

maya-k: posted small table below (id, size, shift):
```
1234, 12, 0.012
7890, 9, 0.011
5555, 20, 0.014
```

ops-bot: perf-run finished — latency p95 unchanged, mem down 18% with int8 bins :sparkles:

eva: thanks! next steps: 1) rerun longtail with alternate sampling (time stratified) 2) per-cluster recall@10 for flagged clusters 3) compare to int4 probe on small subset

samir: +1. also run a tiny eval with AWK-hard negatives (hard_neg=5) to stress recall.

maya-k: will run those overnight and drop results here. thanks :thumbsup:

li-li: if we see consistent >1% drop in recall@10 across longtail, we might need to try hybrid quant (per-channel + outlier handling).

maya-k: noted — will include an experiment with clamp/clip settings and re-run.

eva: ping me tomorrow AM if anything looks odd.

maya-k: done — thanks everyone.
